missed.text: For photometric measurements of a retro-reflective device of Class IA or IB, the illuminating surface itself shall be limited to 100 cm2 though the surfaces of the retro-reflecting optical units need not necessarily attain this area.

When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI values for red retro-reflectors shall be equal to or greater than those in Table 3, expressed in millicandelas per lux, for the angles of divergence and illumination shown.
The trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous flux shall be within the limits for the night-time colours red, amber or white as specified in UN Regulation No. 48.

The lighting and light-signalling devices shall be so fitted that under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which the lighting and light-signalling devices may be subjected, the lighting and light-signalling devices enable the vehicle to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.

The lighting and light-signalling devices shall prevent the lamps from being inadvertently maladjusted under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which the lighting and light-signalling devices may be subjected.
The lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo shall have only two lateral logos (one on each side) or one central logo fitted on the rear of the vehicle.
The lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo shall not include any logos that are not vehicle manufacturer or body manufacturer logos.

When a front or rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with one or more other function(s) which can be switched ON together with them, and the reciprocally incorporated function(s) and the front or rear position lamps are switched ON, the front or rear position lamp shall fulfill the requirements regarding colour of each of these other functions.

The single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.14.11.1., subparagraph (a), the apparent surface of which is composed of two or more distinct parts, shall be installed in such a way that either the total area of the projection of the distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis on a plane tangent to the exterior surface of the outer lens and perpendicular to the reference axis shall occupy not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing the projection of the said apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis; or the minimum distance between the facing edges of two adjacent/tangential distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis shall not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis, except that these requirements shall not apply to a single retro-reflector.

While specific instructions are absent, the lamp shall not intentionally vary its photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface, etc.) during the period when the lamp is switched ON.

Rear position lamps, rear direction-indicator lamps and rear retro-reflectors (triangular or not) may be installed on movable components only if the conditions of paragraph 5.18.1. or 5.18.2. are met.

The lamps (devices) shall be type approved according to the corresponding device Regulations as specified in the relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 6 of this Regulation when installed on a vehicle, where applicable.

The reversing lamp shall be not less than 250 mm and not more than 1,200 mm above the ground, except that for category N2G, N3G, M2G, M3G (off-road) vehicles the maximum height may be increased to 1,400 mm.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles, for S1 or S2 categories devices, the point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
Where the optional lamps are installed, the optional lamps shall be positioned at a height compatible with the requirements of the width and the symmetry of the lamps.

Where optional lamps are installed, the optional lamps shall be positioned at a vertical distance as large as the shape of the bodywork makes it possible, but not less than 600 mm above the mandatory lamps.

The point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the rear position lamp which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle, except that this condition shall not apply to the optional rear lamps.

Where optional rear position lamps are installed, the optional rear position lamps shall be placed at a height compatible with the applicable requirements of paragraph 6.10.4.1. and the symmetry of the lamps.

Where optional rear position lamps are installed, the optional rear position lamps shall be placed at a vertical distance as large as the shape of the bodywork makes it possible, but not less than 600 mm above the mandatory lamps.

Where an optional lamp is mounted above 2,100 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above), the lamp shall have a vertical angle of 15° above and below the horizontal, except that the upward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.

Where a rear side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, for M1 and N1 category vehicles, as an alternative to paragraph 6.10.5.1., at the discretion of the manufacturer or his duly accredited representative, the rear position lamp shall have a horizontal angle of geometric visibility of 45° outwards to 45° inwards; however, where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.
When determining the unobstructed view of the apparent surface of the rear position lamp, the illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light shall be excluded.

The electrical connections for rear position lamps shall be in accordance with paragraph 5.11, except that if a rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a direction-indicator, the electrical connection of the rear position lamp on the relevant side of the vehicle or the reciprocally incorporated part of it may be such that it is switched OFF during the entire time (both ON and OFF cycle) of operation of the direction-indicator lamp.
While daytime running lamps are not switched ON, the rear position lamp shall have a mandatory closed-circuit tell-tale.

When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the limits shall be 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, and 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 7.
The ESA representative of its type shall be tested for immunity to electromagnetic radiation such that test severity in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band are given in Table 2a.

The ESA representative of its type shall be tested for immunity to electromagnetic radiation such that test severity for the minimum test Level over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band is as given in Table 2b.

For the 24 V system starting profile (ISO 16750-2, test level II, 10 pulses), an ESA that shall be operational during engine start phases shall reach functional status class B if it performs immunity-related functions and class D if it does not, and any other ESA shall reach class C, as given in Table 3a; the starting profile applies only to ESAs that may be installed in vehicles with an internal combustion engine started by a 12 V / 24 V starter motor.
Every device belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and other markings as defined in paragraphs 3.3.3.2. to 3.3.3.6.
In the case of front or rear position lamps, front or rear end-outline marker lamps, the arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.
The light source module(s) shall bear the specific identification code of the module where replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.

The specific identification code of the module shall comprise the starting letters “MD” for “MODULE” followed by the approval mark without the circle as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.2.1.1, in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.

Where replaceable light source module(s) is/are used and several non-identical light source modules are used, the specific identification code of the module shall be followed by additional symbols or characters.

The light source module and the lamp shall both have marks from the same applicant, where the approval mark on the light source module does not have to be the same as the one on the lamp in which the module is used, in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The light source module(s) shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The lamp shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.

The position lamps or daytime running lamps, which are reciprocally incorporated with another function, using a common light source, and designed to operate permanently with an additional system to regulate the intensity of the light emitted, shall be permitted.

The logo light emitting surface (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) shall not be required to be symmetrical by itself, notwithstanding the requirements of paragraph 5.5.2. of UN Regulation No. 48, when the internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside of the apparent surface of a lamp (function) incorporates only one manufacturer logo built by transparent or non-transparent components on request of the applicant.
Stop lamps, direction indicator lamps, and reversing lamps shall not incorporate a logo.

If any one light source in a single lamp containing more than one light source fails, then the single lamp shall ensure that at least one of the following provisions applies: (a) the light intensity complies with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution as shown in Annex 3 and when all light sources are illuminated the maximum intensities shall not be exceeded; or (b) a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure, as indicated in paragraphs 6.4.8., 6.7.8., 6.9.8, 6.10.8., 6.11.8., 6.12.8., 6.13.8. and 6.18.8. of UN Regulation No. 48, is produced.
When reversing lamps and manoeuvring lamps are operated for 1 minute and for 10 minutes, the luminous intensities shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.

The luminous intensities for all other lamps (other than those mentioned in 1.2.1), measured after 1 min and either after 30 minutes of operation, or after photometric stability has occurred, shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.

The luminous intensity distribution shall, depending on the light source technology and in addition to paragraph 1, be checked for compliance at the point in time listed in Table A8-1, where the luminous intensity distributions at a point in time may be calculated from the luminous intensity distribution measured according to paragraph 1 by applying at each test point the ratio of luminous intensities measured at the reference coordinate of the lamp (function) under consideration.

extra.text: When the approval mark is affixed to the ESA according to paragraph 5.2. of this Regulation (Model A or Model B), the dimension a of the approval mark shall be 6 mm min.
The ESA shall be tested for conducted emissions.
The ESA shall be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances.
The ESA shall be tested for immunity to conducted disturbances.
The electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA (rear combination lamp) representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 7.

When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the broadband limit in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band shall be 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 6 to this Regulation.
The narrowband electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA (rear combination lamp) representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 8.

When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the narrowband limit in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band shall be 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz.

When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the narrowband limit in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band shall be 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 7.
For vehicles with 12 V systems, the maximum allowed positive pulse amplitude of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA on the supply lines shall be +75 V.
For vehicles with 12 V systems, the maximum allowed negative pulse amplitude of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA on the supply lines shall be -100 V.
For vehicles with 24 V systems, the maximum allowed positive pulse amplitude of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA on the supply lines shall be +150 V.
For vehicles with 24 V systems, the maximum allowed negative pulse amplitude of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA on the supply lines shall be -450 V.
When tested with the stripline method described in Annex 9, the ESA shall be subjected to a test level of 60 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 400 MHz frequency band.
When tested with the stripline method described in Annex 9, the ESA shall be subjected to a minimum test level of 50 V/m over the whole 20 to 400 MHz frequency band.
When tested with the TEM cell method described in Annex 9, the ESA shall be subjected to a test level of 75 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 200 MHz frequency band.
When tested with the TEM cell method described in Annex 9, the ESA shall be subjected to a minimum test level of 62,5 V/m over the whole 20 to 200 MHz frequency band.
When tested with the BCI method described in Annex 9, the ESA shall be subjected to a test level of 60 mA in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 400 MHz frequency band.
When tested with the BCI method described in Annex 9, the ESA shall be subjected to a minimum test level of 50 mA over the whole 20 to 400 MHz frequency band.
When tested with the ALSE method described in Annex 9, the ESA shall be subjected to a test level of 30 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 80 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.
When tested with the ALSE method described in Annex 9, the ESA shall be subjected to a test level of 10 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
When tested with the ALSE method described in Annex 9, the ESA shall be subjected to a minimum test level of 25 V/m over the whole 80 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.
When tested with the ALSE method described in Annex 9, the ESA shall be subjected to a minimum test level of 8 V/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
When tested with the reverberation chamber method described in Annex 9, the ESA shall be subjected to a test level of 21 V/m in over 90 per cent of the LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency band.
When tested with the reverberation chamber method described in Annex 9, the ESA shall be subjected to a test level of 7 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
When tested with the reverberation chamber method described in Annex 9, the ESA shall be subjected to a minimum test level of 18 V/m over the whole LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency band.
When tested with the reverberation chamber method described in Annex 9, the ESA shall be subjected to a minimum test level of 6 V/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
The starting profile test shall be applied to the ESA if it could be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines which are started with a 12V/24V starter motor.

Where the ESA (rear combination lamp) has no immunity related functions, the ESA need not be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.8. and with Annex 9.
The conformity of production procedures shall comply with those set out in Schedule 1 of the 1958 Agreement (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3).
The conformity of production procedures shall meet the following requirements: [the requirements that follow in paragraph 9 of UN R10].

The rear combination lamp (ESA) approved under this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements set forth in paragraph 6. and, if applicable, in paragraph 7. above.

Conformity of production of the component or separate technical unit (ESA) shall be checked on the basis of the data contained in the communication form(s) for type approval set out in Annex 3A and/or 3B to this Regulation, following the procedures of Schedule 1 of the 1958 Agreement (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3).

When the conformity of the rear combination lamp (ESA) taken from the series is being verified, the broadband electromagnetic disturbance levels measured shall not exceed by more than 4 dB (60 per cent) the reference limits prescribed in paragraph 6.5.2.1. and, if applicable, paragraph 7.10.2.1.

When the conformity of the rear combination lamp (ESA) taken from the series is being verified, the narrowband electromagnetic disturbance levels measured shall not exceed by more than 4 dB (60 per cent) the reference limits prescribed in paragraph 6.6.2.1.

When the conformity of the rear combination lamp (ESA) taken from the series is being verified, the ESA shall not exhibit any degradation relating to the direct control of the vehicle which could be observed by the driver or other road user when subjected to a field strength, expressed in Volts/m, up to 80 per cent of the reference limits prescribed in paragraph 6.8.2.1. and, if applicable, paragraph 7.18.2.1.

If the conformity of the rear combination lamp (component or STU) taken from the series is being verified, the component shall show no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions" up to the levels given in paragraph 6.9.1. and, if applicable, paragraph 7.19.1.

If the conformity of the rear combination lamp (component or STU) taken from the series is being verified, the component shall not exceed the conducted emission levels given in paragraph 6.7.1. and, if applicable, paragraph 7.17.1.

The broadband electromagnetic radiation emitted by the ESA (LED light sources and electronics of the rear combination lamp), measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth (see paragraphs 6.5.2.1. and 7.10.2.1.), shall not exceed in the 30-75 MHz frequency band the limit E = 62 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m, where F is the frequency in MHz.

The broadband electromagnetic radiation emitted by the ESA, measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth (see paragraphs 6.5.2.1. and 7.10.2.1.), shall not exceed in the 75-400 MHz frequency band the limit E = 52 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m, where F is the frequency in MHz.

The broadband electromagnetic radiation emitted by the ESA, measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth (see paragraphs 6.5.2.1. and 7.10.2.1.), shall not exceed in the 400-1,000 MHz frequency band the constant limit E = 63 dBµV/m.

When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8 (see paragraph 6.6.2.1.), the narrowband electromagnetic radiation limit of the ESA in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band shall be E = 52 - 25.13 log (F/30) dB microvolts/m, for a 120 kHz bandwidth.

When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8 (see paragraph 6.6.2.1.), the narrowband electromagnetic radiation limit of the ESA in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band shall be E = 42 + 15.13 log (F/75) dB microvolts/m, for a 120 kHz bandwidth.

When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8 (see paragraph 6.6.2.1.), the narrowband electromagnetic radiation limit of the ESA in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band shall remain constant at 53 dB microvolts/m, for a 120 kHz bandwidth.
For the lamp (an ESA powered by LV), a 5 µH / 50 Ω artificial network (AN) as defined in Figure 1 of Appendix 8 shall be used for the emission test.
The AN(s) used for the LV-powered lamp shall be mounted directly on the ground plane.
The grounding connection of the AN(s) used for the LV-powered lamp shall be bonded to the ground plane.
The measurement ports of the AN(s) used for the LV-powered lamp shall be terminated with a 50 Ω load.

The AN impedance ZPB shall correspond to Figure 2 within a tolerance of ± 20 % in the measurement frequency range of 0,1 MHz to 100 MHz, when measured between terminals P and B with a 50 Ω load on the measurement port and with terminals A and B short circuited.
If not otherwise stated in Annex 7, the test measuring broadband electromagnetic emissions from the rear combination lamp ESA shall be performed according to CISPR 25.
The ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load, during the broadband emission test.
For ESA other than involved in "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", the broadband emission test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in Clause 6.4 of CISPR 25.

Measurements of the ambient shall be taken before or after the main test, and in this measurement the extraneous noise or signal shall be at least 6 dB below the limits of interference given in paragraph 6.5.2.1. of this Regulation, except for intentional narrowband ambient transmissions.
The broadband emission limits shall apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS).

If peak detectors are used for the broadband emission measurements, a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 shall be applied to the quasi-peak limits given in paragraphs 6.5. and 7.10. of this Regulation.
The broadband emission measurements shall be performed with a spectrum analyser or a scanning receiver using the parameters defined in Table 1 and Table 2 of Annex 7.

If FFT-based measuring instruments are used, the instruments shall continuously record and evaluate the signal during the measurement time, with a minimum measurement time of 1 s per analysis frequency band (in real-time mode) of the FFT instrument.
If a spectrum analyser is used for peak measurements, the video bandwidth shall be at least three times the resolution bandwidth (RBW).
Unless otherwise specified, the configuration with the LV harness closer to the antenna shall be tested.
The phase centre of the antenna shall be in line with the centre of the longitudinal part of the wiring harnesses for frequencies up to 1,000 MHz.
In the event that the limit is exceeded during the test, investigations shall be made to ensure that this is due to the ESA and not to background radiation.

The maximum of the readings relative to the limit (horizontal/vertical polarization) in each of the 14 frequency bands shall be taken as the characteristic reading at the frequency at which the measurements were made.

When the ESA (rear combination lamp electronics) is tested for radiated broadband emissions on an open area test site according to Annex 7, the test area within the boundary shown in Annex 7, Appendix 1, Figure 1 shall be a level clear area free from electromagnetic reflecting surfaces.
When the narrowband electromagnetic emissions of the ESA are measured according to Annex 8, the test shall be performed according to CISPR 25 if not otherwise stated in Annex 8.
During the narrowband radiated emission tests, the ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.

The narrowband radiated emission test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in paragraph 6.4. of CISPR 25, or alternatively in an open area test site (OATS) which complies with the requirements of CISPR 16-1-4.

Ambient measurements shall be taken before or after the main test, and the extraneous noise or signal shall be at least 6 dB below the limits of interference given in paragraph 6.6.2.1. of this Regulation, except for intentional narrowband ambient transmissions.

The narrowband radiated emission limits shall apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS).
The narrowband radiated emission measurements shall be performed with an average detector.
The narrowband radiated emission measurements shall be performed with a spectrum analyser or a scanning receiver using the parameters defined in Tables 1 and 2 of Annex 8.
When a spectrum analyser is used, the measurement over 30 to 1,000 MHz with the average detector shall use an RBW at -3 dB of 100/120 kHz and a minimum scan time of 100 ms/MHz.
When a scanning receiver is used, the measurement over 30 to 1,000 MHz with the average detector shall use a BW at -6 dB of 120 kHz, a maximum step size of 60 kHz and a minimum dwell time of 5 ms.
If a spectrum analyser is used for peak measurements, the video band width shall be at least three times the resolution band width (RBW).

If FFT-based measuring instruments are used, the FFT-based measuring instruments shall meet the requirements of CISPR 16-1-1 and shall continuously record and evaluate the signal during the measurement time.
If using FFT-based instruments, the minimum measurement time shall be 1 s per analysis frequency band (in real-time mode) of the FFT instrument.

In the event that the limit is exceeded during the test, investigations shall be made to ensure that the exceedance is due to the ESA and not to background radiation including broadband radiation from the ESA.

The maximum of the readings relative to the limit (horizontal/vertical polarisation) in each of the 14 frequency bands shall be taken as the characteristic reading at the frequency at which the measurements were made.

The ESA shall comply with the requirements of any combination of the following test methods at the manufacturer's discretion, provided that the results cover the full frequency range specified in paragraph 3.1. of Annex 9: absorber chamber test according to ISO 11452-2, TEM cell testing according to ISO 11452-3, bulk current injection testing according to ISO 11452-4, stripline testing according to ISO 11452-5, or reverberation chamber test according to ISO 11452-11.
The frequency range and general test conditions for ESA immunity testing shall be based on ISO 11452-1.
The test conditions for the ESA immunity tests shall be according to ISO 11452-1.
The ESA under test shall be switched on and shall be stimulated to be in normal operation condition during the immunity tests.
The ESA under test shall be arranged as defined in Annex 9 unless individual test methods dictate otherwise.
Any extraneous equipment required to operate the ESA under test shall not be in place during the calibration phase.
No extraneous equipment shall be closer than 1 m from the reference point during calibration.
The test signal generating equipment and its layout shall be to the same specification as that used during each appropriate calibration phase.

If the ESA under test consists of more than one unit, the interconnecting cables should ideally be the wiring harnesses as intended for use in the vehicle; if these are not available, the length between the electronic control unit and the AN shall be as defined in the standard.
All cables in the wiring harness of the ESA under test should be terminated as realistically as possible and preferably with real loads and actuators.
The frequency step size and dwell time shall be chosen according to ISO 11452-1.
If the ESA fails the tests defined in Annex 9, it shall be verified as having failed under the relevant test conditions and not as a result of the generation of uncontrolled fields.
When the absorber chamber test is used, the substitution method shall be used to establish the test field conditions according to ISO 11452-2.
When the absorber chamber test is used, the test shall be performed with vertical polarization.
When TEM cell testing is used, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-3.

When bulk current injection testing is used, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-4 on a test bench using either the BCI substitution method with the injection probe positioned at 150 mm distance to the ESA, or the BCI closed loop method with the injection probe positioned at 900 mm distance to the ESA.

As an alternative, when the ESA is tested while installed in the vehicle, the BCI test shall be performed according to ISO 11451-4 with the substitution method and injection probe positioned at 150 mm distance to the ESA.
When stripline testing is used, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-5.
When the reverberation chamber test is used, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-11.
Unless otherwise specified, the reverberation chamber testing method shall be carried out using a test setup with ground plane.
The rear combination lamp ESA shall be immune to conducted transients on the vehicle power supply when tested according to the method of Annex 10.
The rear combination lamp ESA shall limit conducted transients from the ESA to the vehicle power supply when tested according to the method of Annex 10.

The emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA on 12/24 V supply lines shall be measured according to the International Standard ISO 7637-2 on supply lines as well as on other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
The rear combination lamp belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and other markings as defined in paragraphs 3.3.3.2. to 3.3.3.6.
The approval marking shall consist of the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
The approval marking shall include the four to six-digit sequential number being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2.
The approval marking shall include the symbols identifying the light signalling lamps prescribed in paragraph 3.2.4.
The approval marking shall include the number of this Regulation followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
In the case of rear position lamps, the horizontal arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.
If applicable, the additional letter "D" shall be placed to the right side of the symbol mentioned in paragraph 3.2.4. on lamps which may be used as part of an assembly of two independent lamps.
If applicable, the additional letter "Y" shall be placed to the right side of the symbol mentioned in paragraph 3.2.4. on lamps which are used as part of an interdependent lamps system.
On lamps with reduced light distribution (see paragraph 1.1. of Annex 3), the approval marking shall include a vertical arrow starting from a horizontal segment and directed downwards.

An electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control being part of the lamp, but not included into the lamp body, shall be marked with its identification number and the name of the manufacturer.
Where a single approval mark is affixed on the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, it shall be visible after their installation.

Where a single approval mark is affixed on the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, no part of the lamps that transmits light shall be removable without at the same time removing the approval mark.
The conformity of production procedures for the rear combination lamp shall comply with those set out in the 1958 Agreement, Schedule 1 (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3).
The conformity of production procedures for the rear combination lamp shall comply with the requirements set forth in paragraph 6.
Each lamp submitted for approval (rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp) shall conform to the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4. and 5.

The requirements contained in sections 5 "General specifications" and 6 "Individual specifications" (and in the Annexes referenced in the said sections) of UN Regulation No. 48, and its series of amendments in force at the time of application for the lamp type approval, shall apply to the rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and retro-reflector of the rear combination lamp.

The requirements of UN Regulation No. 48 pertinent to each lamp function and to vehicle category M1, on which the lamp is intended to be installed, shall be applied where their verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.

The lamps (rear position, stop and reversing lamps) shall be so designed and constructed that in normal conditions of use, and notwithstanding the vibrations to which the lamps may be subjected in such use, the lamps retain the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation.

If the rear position lamp or stop lamp is type approved as an assembly of two independent lamps marked "D", this shall be applied only to front and rear position lamps, stop lamps, front and rear end-outline marker lamps, daytime running lamps and direction indicator lamps (not to the reversing lamp).

If the rear position lamp or stop lamp is type approved as an interdependent lamp system marked "Y", this shall be applied only to front and rear position lamps, stop lamps, front and rear end-outline marker lamps, daytime running lamps and direction indicator lamps (not to the reversing lamp).
The stop lamp shall not incorporate a logo.
The reversing lamp shall not incorporate a logo.

In a single lamp containing more than one light source, a group of light sources wired so that the failure of any one of them causes all of them to stop emitting light shall be considered to be one light source.

In case of failure of any one light source in the rear position lamp containing more than one light source, either the light intensity shall comply with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution as shown in Annex 3, with the maximum intensities not exceeded when all light sources are illuminated, or a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure as indicated in paragraph 6.10.8. of UN Regulation No. 48 shall be produced.

In case of failure of any one light source in the stop lamp containing more than one light source, either the light intensity shall comply with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution as shown in Annex 3, with the maximum intensities not exceeded when all light sources are illuminated, or a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure as indicated in paragraph 6.7.8. of UN Regulation No. 48 shall be produced.

In case of failure of any one light source in the reversing lamp containing more than one light source, either the light intensity shall comply with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution as shown in Annex 3, with the maximum intensities not exceeded when all light sources are illuminated, or a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure as indicated in paragraph 6.4.8. of UN Regulation No. 48 shall be produced.

If the rear position lamp is of category R2 emitting more than the maximum value of category R1, in case of failure of the variable intensity control the requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically.

If the stop lamp is of category S2 emitting more than the maximum value of category S1, in case of failure of the variable intensity control the requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically.
In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the design of the lamp shall be such that the light source(s) can be fixed in no other position but the correct one.

In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the light source(s) holder shall conform to the characteristics given in IEC Publication 60061, the holder data sheet relevant to the category of light source(s) prescribed applying.

In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), where a category of LED substitute light source(s) is also prescribed, the light source(s) holder shall conform to the holder data sheet of IEC Publication 60061 relevant to the category of LED substitute light source(s).

During the water spray test, drain wicks, when used, shall be tested in the device.
During the water spray test, the device shall be rotated about its vertical axis at a rate of 4.0 ± 0.5 min-1.

Since the retro-reflector is reciprocally incorporated or grouped with signalling or lighting functions, the rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions shall be operated at design voltage during the water spray test according to a cycle of 5 min ON, 55 min OFF.
The water spray test shall last 12 hours (12 cycles of 5/55 min).
After the water spray test, the rotation and the water spray shall be turned OFF and the device allowed to drain for 1 hour with the cabinet door closed.
Upon completion of the drain period, the interior of the device shall be observed for moisture accumulation.
Upon completion of the drain period, no standing pool of water shall be formed in the interior of the device, nor shall one be formed by tapping or tilting the device.
After the moisture test, the RI shall be measured according to the method specified in Part 1 of Annex 4 after having dried the exterior of the device with a dry cotton cloth.
The interior of the dust exposure test chamber shall be cubical in shape in size 0.9 to 1.5 m per side, with an internal volume, not including a hopper shaped bottom, of 2 m3 maximum.
The dust exposure test chamber shall be charged with 3 to 5 kg of the test dust.
The dust exposure test chamber shall have the capability of agitating the test dust by means of compressed air or blower fans in such a way that the dust is diffused throughout the chamber.
The test dust used shall be fine powdered cement in accordance with standard ASTM C 150-84.
The sample device shall be mounted on a test fixture with the initial RI measured and recorded before being exposed to dust.
During the dust exposure test, all drain holes and other openings of the device shall remain open.
During the dust exposure test, drain wicks, when used, shall be tested in the device.
The mounted device shall be placed in the dust chamber no closer than 150 mm from a wall.
If the device has a length exceeding 600 mm, it shall be horizontally centred in the test chamber.

The test dust shall be agitated as completely as possible by compressed air or blower(s) at intervals of 15 min for a period of 2 to 15 s for the duration of 5 hours, and the dust shall be allowed to settle between the agitation periods.

Upon completion of the dust exposure test, the exterior of the device shall be cleaned and dried with a dry cotton cloth and the RI measured according to the method specified in paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation.

As the retro-reflector is combined with a lamp, the rear combination lamp shall be stripped of all removable parts and subjected to the action of a saline mist for a period of 50 hours, comprising two periods of exposure of 24 hours each, separated by an interval of two hours during which the sample is allowed to dry.

After the corrosion test, the coefficient of retro-reflection RA of the retro-reflective areas, when measured after a recovery period of 48 hours as specified in Part 2 of Annex 6, at an entrance angle of β2 = 5° and an observation angle of α = 20', shall be not less than the value in Table 9.

After the corrosion test, the coefficient of retro-reflection RA of the retro-reflective areas, when measured after a recovery period of 48 hours as specified in Part 2 of Annex 6, at an entrance angle of β2 = 5° and an observation angle of α = 20', shall be not more than the value in Table 10.
Before measuring the coefficient of retro-reflection after the corrosion test, the surface of the retro-reflector shall be cleaned to remove salt deposits from the saline mist.

If the retro-reflector is a mirror-backed moulded plastics reflector of Class IA or IB with an accessible rear face, the reverse side of the retro-reflective device shall be brushed with a hard nylon brush.

After brushing the rear face of a mirror-backed moulded plastics retro-reflector of Class IA or IB, a cotton cloth soaked in the mixture defined in Part 1 of Annex 7 shall be applied to the said rear face for one minute, then removed and the retro-reflective device left to dry.
As soon as evaporation is completed, the reverse side of the mirror-backed retro-reflective device shall be brushed with the same hard nylon brush as before.

After the rear-face resistance test, the RI of the mirror-backed retro-reflective device shall be measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation, after the whole surface of the mirror-backed rear face has been covered with Indian ink.
The accelerated artificial weathering apparatus shall be in accordance with EN ISO 4892-1:2016 and EN ISO 4892-2:2013.
The accelerated artificial weathering apparatus shall be capable to control temperature and relative humidity.
The accelerated artificial weathering apparatus shall be equipped with a water spray system.
The water spray system of the weathering apparatus shall be capable to spray a minimum of 0.3 ml/cm² within 5 minutes.
The spray water used in the accelerated artificial weathering test shall be in accordance to the requirements of EN ISO 4892-2:2013.
For temperature measurement in the accelerated artificial weathering test, either a Black-Standard thermometer (test method TM1) or a Black-Panel thermometer (test method TM2) shall be used.
The weathering test method used (TM1 or TM2) shall be specified in the test report.
Retro-reflective devices shall be exposed to accelerated artificial weathering for a period of 500 hours.

When test method TM2 (Black-panel thermometer, cycle No. 4 according to EN ISO 4892-2:2013) is used, the exposure cycle shall be 102 min dry at a broadband irradiance (300 to 400 nm) of 60 ± 2 W/m², narrowband irradiance (340 nm) of 0.51 ± 0.02 W/m², black-panel temperature of 63 ± 3 °C and relative humidity of 50 ± 10 %, followed by 18 min water spray at a broadband irradiance of 60 ± 2 W/m² and narrowband irradiance of 0.51 ± 0.02 W/m².
Preparation of retro-reflector test specimens for the weathering test shall be in accordance with the general guidelines given in EN ISO 4892-2:2013.
For the resistance to fuels test of the retro-reflective device, a test mixture of 70 vol. per cent of n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent of toluol shall be applied.

In the resistance to fuels test, the outer surface of the retro-reflective device and, in particular, of the illuminating surface, shall be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in the test mixture of 70 vol. per cent of n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent of toluol.
About five minutes after wiping with the test mixture, the surface of the retro-reflective device shall be inspected visually.
After the resistance to fuels test, the surface of the retro-reflective device must not show any apparent surface changes, except that slight surface cracks will not be objected to.

In the case of moulded plastics reflectors of Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB or IVA, the outer surface of the retro-reflective device and, in particular, the illuminating surface, shall be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in a detergent lubricating oil.

In the case of moulded plastics reflectors of Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB or IVA, the surface of the retro-reflective device wiped with detergent lubricating oil shall be cleaned after about 5 minutes.

In the case of moulded plastics reflectors of Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB or IVA, after the lubricating oil exposure and cleaning, the RI of the retro-reflective device shall be measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation.
The approval number of the retro-reflective device shall be placed close to, but in any position in relation to, the circle surrounding the letter "E".
The digits constituting the approval number of the retro-reflective device shall face the same way as the "E".
The group of symbols indicating the class of the retro-reflective device shall be diametrically opposite the approval number.
The lighting and light-signalling devices shall be so fitted that it is not possible for the lamps to be inadvertently maladjusted.

In the absence of specific instructions, the height and orientation of the rear combination lamp (rear position, stop and reversing lamps and retro-reflector) shall be verified with the vehicle unladen and placed on a flat, horizontal surface, in the condition defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2.

In the absence of specific instructions, the rear combination lamps constituting a pair (left- and right-hand side) shall be fitted to the vehicle symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane, this estimate being based on the exterior geometrical form of the lamp and not on the edge of its illuminating surface referred to in paragraph 2.10.3.

In the absence of specific instructions, the rear combination lamps constituting a pair shall be symmetrical to one another in relation to the median longitudinal plane; this requirement is not valid with regard to the interior structure of the lamp.

In the absence of specific instructions, the lamps of the same function constituting a pair (rear position lamps, stop lamps, reversing lamps and retro-reflectors) shall satisfy the same colorimetric requirements.
On vehicles whose external shape is asymmetrical, the installation requirements of paragraph 5.5 (symmetrical installation of the paired rear lamp functions) shall be satisfied so far as is possible.

When a rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with one or more other function(s) which can be switched ON together with it, the requirements regarding colour of each of these other functions shall be fulfilled when the reciprocally incorporated function(s) and the rear position lamps are switched ON.

Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.14.11.1., subparagraph (a), the apparent surface of which is composed of two or more distinct parts, shall be installed in such a way that either (a) the total area of the projection of the distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis on a plane tangent to the exterior surface of the outer lens and perpendicular to the reference axis occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing the projection of the said apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis; or (b) the minimum distance between the facing edges of two adjacent/tangential distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis does not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis.

The maximum height above the ground of the rear combination lamp functions (rear position, stop, reversing lamp and retro-reflector) shall be measured from the highest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis.

The minimum height above the ground of the rear combination lamp functions (rear position, stop, reversing lamp and retro-reflector) shall be measured from the lowest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis.
For the purposes of reducing the geometric visibility angles, the position of the lamp with regard to height above the ground shall be measured from the H plane.

When referred to the overall width, the position of the lamp as regards width shall be determined from the edge of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis which is furthest from the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle.
When referred to the distance between lamps, the position of the lamp as regards width shall be determined from the inner edges of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis.

In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface, etc.) of the rear position lamp shall not be intentionally varied during the period when the lamp is switched ON.

In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface, etc.) of the stop lamp shall not be intentionally varied during the period when the lamp is switched ON.

In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface, etc.) of the reversing lamp shall not be intentionally varied during the period when the lamp is switched ON.

For the visibility of red light towards the front of the vehicle, there shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of a red lamp (rear position lamp, stop lamp, retro-reflector) if viewed by an observer moving within Zone 1 in a transverse plane situated 25 m in front of the vehicle (see Annex 4).

The requirement for simultaneous switching of the rear position lamps with the front position lamps, end-outline marker lamps, side-marker lamps and rear registration plate lamp need not be met while one or more of the following conditions exist: (a) front and rear position lamps, as well as side-marker lamps when combined or reciprocally incorporated with said lamps, are switched ON as parking lamps; (b) side-marker lamps flash in conjunction with direction indicators; (c) daytime running lamps are switched ON; (d) the front position lamps function is substituted under the provisions of paragraph 5.12.1.
The colour of the light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
The colour of the light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
The colour of the light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
The colour of the light reflected by the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be red.
The number of lamps mounted on the vehicle shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of this Regulation.

If the rear position lamp or rear retro-reflector is installed on a movable component, the lamps on the movable component shall meet all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for those lamps at all fixed positions of the movable component.

Where the rear position lamp or rear retro-reflector of the rear combination lamp is fitted as an additional lamp for the functions referred to in paragraph 5.18. and is switched ON when the movable component is in any fixed open position, it shall satisfy all the position, geometric visibility and photometric requirements applicable to the lamps installed on the movable component.

When the rear combination lamp is installed on a movable component and the movable component is in the "normal position(s) of use", the lamp shall always return to the position(s) specified by the manufacturer in accordance with this Regulation.

The apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the rear position lamp shall not be hidden more than 50 per cent by any movable component, with or without a light-signalling device installed on it, in any fixed position (stable or natural rest position(s) specified by the vehicle manufacturer, whether locked or not) different from the "normal position of use".

The apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the retro-reflector shall not be hidden more than 50 per cent by any movable component, with or without a light-signalling device installed on it, in any fixed position (stable or natural rest position(s) specified by the vehicle manufacturer, whether locked or not) different from the "normal position of use".

If the 50 per cent obscuration requirement of paragraph 5.21 is not practicable for the rear position lamp, additional lamps satisfying all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for rear position lamps shall be switched ON when the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the rear position lamp is more than 50 per cent hidden by the movable component.

If the 50 per cent obscuration requirement of paragraph 5.21 is not practicable for the retro-reflector, additional devices satisfying all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for retro-reflectors shall be provided and effective when the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the retro-reflector is more than 50 per cent hidden by the movable component.

If neither paragraph 5.21 nor 5.21.1 is practicable for the rear position lamp, a notice in the vehicle shall inform the user that in certain position(s) of the movable components other road users shall be warned of the presence of the vehicle on the road, for example by means of a warning triangle or other devices according to national requirements for use on the road; this alternative does not apply to retro-reflectors.

With the exception of the retro-reflector, each lamp of the rear combination lamp (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp), even bearing an approval mark, shall be capable of being made to operate by the sole installation of a light source and/or a fuse; otherwise it is deemed not to be present.

If the rear combination lamp is approved with light source(s) according to UN Regulation No. 37, except when such light sources are used as non-replaceable light source(s) as defined in paragraph 2.9.1.2., the lamp shall be fitted in the vehicle in such a way that the light source can be correctly replaced without the need for expert assistance and without the need for special tools, other than those provided with the vehicle by the manufacturer.

If the rear combination lamp is approved with light source(s) according to UN Regulation No. 37, except when such light sources are used as non-replaceable light source(s), the vehicle manufacturer shall provide with the vehicle a detailed description of the procedure for replacement of the light source.

Where a light source module of the rear combination lamp includes a holder for an approved replaceable light source according to Regulation No. 37, this light source shall be replaceable as required in paragraph 5.23., without the need for expert assistance and without the need for special tools other than those provided with the vehicle by the manufacturer.

If a temporary fail-safe replacement of the light-signalling function of the rear position lamp is used, the replacement function in case of a failure shall be similar in colour to the rear position lamp function that has ceased to operate.

If a temporary fail-safe replacement of the light-signalling function of the rear position lamp is used, the replacement function in case of a failure shall be similar in main intensity to the rear position lamp function that has ceased to operate.

If a temporary fail-safe replacement of the light-signalling function of the rear position lamp is used, the replacement function in case of a failure shall be similar in position to the rear position lamp function that has ceased to operate.
If a temporary fail-safe replacement of the light-signalling function of the rear position lamp is used, the replacement device shall remain operational in its original safety function.

During temporary fail-safe replacement of the light-signalling function of the rear position lamp, a tell-tale on the dashboard (paragraph 2.3.5. of this Regulation) shall indicate occurrence of a temporary replacement and need for repair.

If the rear position lamp of category R2 and the stop lamp of category S2 are provided with variable luminous intensity control responding simultaneously to one or more of the conditions listed in paragraphs 5.26.1. and 5.26.2., then the intensity of these lamps, when combined, grouped or reciprocally incorporated, shall vary all together in the same manner and in a similar proportion.

If the rear position lamp of category R2 and the stop lamp of category S2 have variable luminous intensity control, then in the entire intensity range the specific prescribed ratio between the luminous intensities of the two lamps, if applicable, shall be maintained throughout variation transitions.

If the luminous intensity of the rear position lamp (R2) or stop lamp (S2) is increased or decreased in relation to ambient lighting, fog, snowfall, rain, spray, dust clouds or contamination of the light emitting surface, then the variation shall remain within the limits prescribed in the pertinent UN Regulations.

Independent from environmental conditions, a decrease of the luminous intensity of the rear position lamp (R2) and stop lamp (S2) shall only be activated, within the limits prescribed in the pertinent UN Regulations, when the vehicle speed is equal or less than 20 km/h or the distance to the following vehicle is equal or less than 20 m.
A traffic-condition intensity decrease already activated for the rear position lamp (R2) and stop lamp (S2) shall not remain active when the vehicle speed exceeds 50 km/h.
No sharp variation of intensity of the rear position lamp and stop lamp shall be observed during transition of the variable luminous intensity.

When the electrical system of the vehicle is in a constant voltage operating condition representative for the M1 category, the voltage supplied at the terminals of the rear combination lamp functions, if they have been tested according to their type approval documentation by the application of a special power supply/electronic light source control gear, or in a secondary operating mode or at a voltage requested by the applicant, shall not exceed the voltage specified for the relevant devices or functions as they have been approved. This does not apply if the device includes an electronic light source control gear, a variable intensity control being part of the device, or only light source(s) approved according to UN Regulation No. 128.

In all cases of electric power supply conditions not covered by paragraph 5.27.1., the voltage at the terminals of the rear combination lamp device(s) or function(s) shall not exceed 6.75 V (6 Volt-Systems), 13.5 V (12 Volt-Systems) or 28 V (24 Volt-Systems) by more than 3 per cent, when the electrical system of the vehicle is in a constant voltage operating condition representative for the M1 category. This does not apply if the device includes an electronic light source control gear, a variable intensity control being part of the device, or only light source(s) approved according to UN Regulation No. 128.
The means of controlling the maximum voltage at the terminals of the rear combination lamp may, for convenience, be located within the body of the device.
If geometric visibility measurements are taken closer to the lamp, the direction of observation shall be shifted parallel to achieve the same accuracy.

If, when the lamp is installed, any part of the apparent surface of the lamp is hidden by any further parts of the vehicle, proof shall be furnished that the part of the lamp not hidden by obstacles still conforms to the photometric values prescribed for the approval of the device.
A LED module of the rear combination lamp may be non-replaceable only if this is stated in the communication sheet of the component type approval.

The rear combination lamp (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and retro-reflector functions), when installed on a vehicle, shall, where applicable, be type approved according to the corresponding device Regulations as specified in the relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 6 of this Regulation.
If the light-signalling lamp incorporates a manufacturer logo, the lamp shall be type approved according to the requirements of UN Regulation No. 148.
The reversing lamp shall be mandatory on motor vehicles.
On motor vehicles of category M1, one reversing lamp device shall be mandatory and a second device shall be optional.
The reversing lamp shall be positioned in height not less than 250 mm and not more than 1,200 mm above the ground.
For a reversing lamp installed at the rear of the vehicle, the geometric visibility defined by angle α as specified in paragraph 2.10.7. shall be 15° upwards and 5° downwards.
If there is only one reversing lamp device installed at the rear of the vehicle, the geometric visibility angle β as specified in paragraph 2.10.7. shall be 45° to right and to left.
If there are two reversing lamp devices installed at the rear of the vehicle, the geometric visibility angle β as specified in paragraph 2.10.7. shall be 45° outwards and 30° inwards.
The reversing lamp shall be oriented rearwards.
A tell-tale for the reversing lamp is optional; however a tell-tale indicating failure shall be mandatory if required by the component regulation.
Stop lamp devices of S1 or S2 categories shall be mandatory on M1 category vehicles.

For M1 category vehicles, the point on the apparent surface of the S1 or S2 category stop lamp in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
The S1 or S2 category stop lamp shall be positioned at the rear of the vehicle in length.
For S1 and S2 category stop lamps mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward horizontal angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.
Where the S1 or S2 category stop lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward vertical angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
The stop lamp shall be oriented towards the rear of the vehicle.
The stop lamps need not function if the device which starts and/or stops the propulsion system is in a position that makes it impossible for the propulsion system to operate.
A tell-tale indicating failure of the stop lamp shall be provided if required by the component regulation; otherwise the tell-tale is optional.
The rear position lamps (devices of R or R1 or R2 categories) shall be mandatory on the vehicle.
The number of rear position lamps shall be two.
The rear position lamps shall be type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

In width, that point on the apparent surface of the rear position lamp in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
In length, the rear position lamp shall be located at the rear of the vehicle.

For M1 category vehicles, as an alternative to paragraph 6.10.5.1., at the discretion of the manufacturer and only if a rear side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, the horizontal angle of geometric visibility of the rear position lamp shall be 45° outwards to 45° inwards; where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.
The rear position lamp shall be oriented rearwards.
The electrical connections of the rear position lamp shall be in accordance with paragraph 5.11.
The rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be mandatory on motor vehicles.

Additional retro-reflecting devices and materials (including two retro-reflectors not complying with paragraph 6.14.4.) shall be permitted only provided they do not impair the effectiveness of the mandatory lighting and light-signalling devices.
In height, the rear retro-reflector shall be not less than 250 mm above the ground.

In height, the rear retro-reflector shall be not more than 900 mm above the ground, or not more than 1,200 mm if grouped with any rear lamp(s), or 1,500 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 900 mm or 1,200 mm respectively.
In length, the rear retro-reflector shall be at the rear of the vehicle.
The rear retro-reflector shall be oriented rearwards.
Any vehicle approved pursuant to this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements set out in paragraphs 5. and 6. above.

When verifying, according to paragraph 5.10.4., that no red light from the rear combination lamp is visible to the front and no white light other than from the reversing lamp is visible to the rear, the zones 1 and 2 explored by the eye of the observer shall be bounded in height by two horizontal planes 1 m and 2.2 m respectively above the ground.

When verifying visibility of a red lamp to the front and of a white lamp to the rear, the zones 1 and 2 shall be bounded in width by two vertical planes that form, to the front and to the rear respectively, an angle of 15° outwards from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane. These planes shall pass through the point or points of contact of vertical planes parallel to the vehicle's median longitudinal plane that delimit the vehicle's overall width.

If there are several points of contact delimiting the vehicle's overall width, the foremost point shall correspond to the forward plane and the rearmost point to the rearward plane bounding the visibility zones.

The position of the rear position, stop and reversing lamps and retro-reflector of the rear combination lamp, in width, in height and in length, shall be checked in accordance with the general requirements set out in paragraphs 2.10.2., 2.10.3., 2.10.4., 2.3.3. and 5.4. of this Regulation, and the values measured for the distances shall be such that the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled.

The angles of geometric visibility of the rear position, stop and reversing lamps and retro-reflector shall be checked in accordance with paragraph 2.10.7. of this Regulation, and the values measured for the angles shall be such that the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled, except that the limits of the angles may have an allowance corresponding to the ±3º variation permitted in paragraph 5.3. for the mounting of the light-signalling devices.
The visibility of red light from the rear position lamp, stop lamp and retro-reflector towards the front shall be checked in accordance with paragraph 5.10. of this Regulation.
The visibility of white light towards the rear shall be checked in accordance with paragraph 5.10. of this Regulation.
The electrical connections of the rear combination lamp shall be checked by switching on every lamp supplied by the electrical system of the vehicle.

The rear position, stop and reversing lamps and their tell-tales shall function in accordance with the provisions set out in paragraphs 5.11. to 5.14. of this Regulation and with the individual specifications applicable to each lamp.

The presence, number, colour, arrangement and, where applicable, the category of the rear position, stop and reversing lamps and retro-reflector shall be checked by visual inspection of the lamps and their markings, and shall be such that the requirements set out in paragraphs 5.15. and 5.16. as well as in the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled.
